title: Linking congruence Sigma_1 ≡ p (mod p^2) imported from cited thm:iiiiv; needs elementary proof

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** Section 3, Theorem `thm:link`, proof of the congruence $\Sigma_1\equiv p\pmod{p^2}$ (it invokes `thm:iiiiv`(2)/(1) plus integrality of $E_{p-3},B_{p-3}$).

**Gap.** The *algebraic* identity $\Sigma_1=S_0+3S_1$ is proved correctly. But the *congruence* $\Sigma_1\equiv p\pmod{p^2}$ — equivalently the linking relation $3S_1\equiv p-S_0\pmod{p^2}$ used for part (ii) and for the refutation of (i.2) — is obtained only as the mod-$p^2$ shadow of the cited deep `thm:iiiiv`. Thus the linking relation is conditional on an unproved theorem.

**Consequence for the abstract's claim.** The abstract states the refutation of (i.2) is "unconditional". As written it is not: it depends on (a) the value of $S_0$ from the cited `thm:S0` (see separate issue) and (b) $\Sigma_1\equiv p\pmod{p^2}$ from the cited `thm:iiiiv`.

**What must be proved.** Supply an ELEMENTARY mod-$p^2$ proof of $\Sigma_1=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3/16^k\equiv p\pmod{p^2}$, independent of the third-order machinery. Candidate routes: (i) WZ/creative-telescoping for $(3k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^3$ reduced mod $p^2$; or (ii) a direct mod-$p^2$ evaluation of $S_1$ combined with the (separately needed) value of $S_0$. Closing this makes the refutation genuinely unconditional as claimed. Numerics confirm $\Sigma_1\equiv p\pmod{p^2}$ for all $p\le 100$.
